title: Shard-aware prefetch iterator for embeddings client (typed responses, robust pagination)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Large-scale reranking and embedding workloads are showing two classes of user friction: (1) tail latency when fetching large result sets across sharded vector backends, and (2) brittle client behavior when a single item in a paginated request fails (partial failures). Current SDK pagination is sequential and exposes a weakly-typed unstructured response that makes robust error handling and typed introspection harder in Python/TS clients.

Goal: Deliver a new client iterator that is shard-aware and does bounded prefetch for adjacent pages, returns strongly typed EmbeddingResponse objects (vector, metadata, model_version, optional rerank_score), and exposes deterministic monotonic cursors that allow safe retrying and resume after partial failures. The iterator must support both sync and async idioms in Python and TS, integrate with Abort/Cancel APIs, and fail gracefully when prefetch is disabled or server shard hints are absent.

Non-goals: Changing server-side routing or shard placement; changing on-disk vector store formats; implementing new reranking algorithms (we only surface scores provided by the rerank endpoint).
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes EmbeddingIterator (sync + async) in Python and TS that yields EmbeddingResponse typed objects
Iterator performs bounded prefetch (configurable prefetch_pages, default=2) and respects a max_memory_pages limit
Cursor format is monotonic and backwards-compatible: server returns cursor_v2 when available; iterator falls back to cursor_v1 mapping when not

Partial failures: single-item failures are returned as per-item error objects (EmbeddingItemError) while iterator continues delivering successful items; overall call returns non-200 only for global failures
95th percentile end-to-end latency for embedding pagination (page_size=64, concurrent queries=200) improves by >=30% in canary compared to control
Client unit tests + integration tests (local shard simulator) covering cancelation, retry-on-resume, partial-failure semantics, and type contracts
Backward compatible: existing simple paginated API still works when prefetch is disabled or older server does not send shard hints
Documentation updated with migration guide and examples for Python and TS
Telemetry emits prefetch_hit, prefetch_miss, partial_failure_count, cursor_upgrade_count
implementation_notes: Server message change: add optional 'shard_hint' and 'cursor_v2' fields to paginated responses; server will not reject clients that ignore these fields
Client: new EmbeddingResponse type (fields: id, vector, metadata, model_version, rerank_score?, status) and EmbeddingItemError (id, code, message)
Python surface: EmbeddingIterator (iterator + async iterator) + EmbeddingClient.prefetch_config param; uses asyncio.Semaphore to bound concurrent prefetch requests
TS surface: AsyncIterable<EmbeddingResponse | EmbeddingItemError> and sync Iterator wrapper for Node usage; integrates AbortSignal for cancellation
Cursor handling: expose cursor_v2 token string; implement client-side translator for older cursor_v1 when server advertises 'cursor_compat' metadata
Backpressure: iterator should stop issuing prefetch when consumer falls more than 3 pages behind; prefetch semantics are advisory and cancelable
Memory safety: prefetch queue holds only serialized EmbeddingResponse bytes until consumer consumes; provide max_memory_pages config
Error handling: per-page HTTP 200 with item-level error details; if server returns non-200 the iterator surfaces a final exception after draining successful buffered items
Feature flag: rollout controlled by 'sdk.prefetch_shard_aware' flag in feature service for staged rollout
Add e2e canary against dedicated canary cluster that simulates 8 shards, heavy skew, and network jitter
risks: Shard hints may leak topology that we must ensure contains no sensitive data — design restricts hint to opaque shard_id string
Prefetch increases load on vector backends if client usage is unbounded; mitigate with conservative defaults and server-side per-client rate limits
Complexity for consumers: too many knobs could cause misuse — keep defaults simple and document patterns
Migration risk when cursor formats change; provide server-side compat and client automatic fallbacks
Typed contract drift: must keep EmbeddingResponse stable across minor releases; introduce fields only as optional
test_plan: Unit tests for iterator state machine (prefetch queue, backpressure, abort) in Python and TS
Integration test with local shard-simulator repo (https://github.com/redwood-inference/vec-shard-sim) that validates latency and correctness under skew
Chaos test: inject 10% per-item failures and validate partial failures are surfaced as EmbeddingItemError while overall iterator continues
Benchmark harness: use embedding-loadbench to compare 95p latency with and without prefetch across 10k requests
Type tests: run mypy/typecheck and TS strict mode for typed response surfaces
Canary rollout: enable feature flag for 5% of hosted traffic for 72 hours, compare telemetry metrics
rollout_plan: Feature branch and review: target PR to rw-emb-sdk main; include opt-in flag defaulting to off
Internal dogfood: enable for dataset-indexing team (team-data-index) for 1 week
Canary: flip 'sdk.prefetch_shard_aware' to 5% for hosted API consumers on runtime-1.23 canary cluster
Monitor: observe prefetch_hit/miss, partial_failure_count, 95p latency, error budgets; rollback if partial_failure_count increases >2x
GA: enable by default in next minor SDK release (runtime-1.23+), publish migration guide and changelog
